title: ServiceNow QA Automation Engineer
description:
BETSOL is a cloud-first digital transformation and data management company offering products and IT services to enterprises in over 40 countries. BETSOL team holds several engineering patents, is recognized with industry awards, and BETSOL maintains a net promoter score that is 2x the industry average.
BETSOL’s open source backup and recovery product line, Zmanda (Zmanda.com), delivers up to 50% savings in total cost of ownership (TCO) and best-in-class performance.
BETSOL Global IT Services (BETSOL.com) builds and supports end-to-end enterprise solutions, reducing time-to-market for its customers.

We take pride in being an employee-centric organization, offering comprehensive health insurance, competitive salaries, volunteer programs, and scholarship opportunities. Office amenities include a fitness center, cafe, and recreational facilities.
Learn more at betsol.com

BETSOL's team designs and runs software license tracking on ServiceNow SAM Professional. For each software publisher brought into scope, the team analyses contracts, models entitlements and consumption, and delivers a custom publisher view and dashboard that shows licenses owned, licenses consumed and the resulting compliance position. The publishers we work with span SaaS and enterprise software, each with its own license metrics, SKUs and data sources. 
We are looking for a QA engineer who can test ServiceNow SAM implementation end to end and keep growing the test automation. You will validate the calculations behind every license number, to prove that dashboards match the underlying report data, and turn repeatable checks into automated scripts so that releases move from development to UAT to production quickly. You will work closely with ServiceNow developers, business analysts and project managers, and with business stakeholders during UAT. 
Key responsibilities 
Testing SAM publisher implementations 
- Review publisher analysis and stories, then write test scenarios and test cases that trace back to the agreed requirements and expected dashboard output. 
- Validate entitlement and consumption logic: rights owned, rights consumed, rights available and rights needed, license metrics (for example User Subscription versus Resource Consumption) and custom SKUs created for usage that standard SKUs do not cover. 
- Verify calculation rules such as contract term calculation with date tolerance, unit price by billing frequency, weighted average price across entitlements and ratchet behaviour where increases are applied and decreases are not. 
- Test server-side components on the custom SAM report table, including business rules, script includes, scheduled jobs that run by product group, and audit and data-fix scripts. 
- Reconcile dashboard values against report and source records for each product group, and validate data built from vendor exports and admin API extracts (deduplication, scoping by site and contract line). 
- Run functional, regression and UAT support cycles across the development, test and production instances. 
Building and running test automation 
- Extend the existing SAM automation framework and test scripts, and deliver items on the SAM test automation roadmap against agreed timelines. 
- Automate regression suites for recurring publisher patterns so developers can run them when QA capacity is tight. 
- Use the ServiceNow Automated Test Framework (ATF) and server-side scripts to automate data and calculation checks. 
- Keep scripts maintainable, documented and reusable across publishers. 
Quality process and reporting 
- Log, track and retest defects; record evidence and keep test case documents current. 
- Produce a QA sign-off document for each release with test case counts, pass results, defects raised and fixes verified, before promotion to UAT. 
- Support stakeholder reviews of dashboards before production, and fold their feedback into validation before deployment. 
- Take part in sprint ceremonies, estimate QA effort and raise risks to delivery early.

Required qualifications 
- Minimum 2 years of hands-on QA experience on the ServiceNow platform, within at least 3 years of overall software testing experience. 
- Working knowledge of ServiceNow SAM Professional or Software Asset Management concepts: entitlements, license metrics, software models, reconciliation and compliance. 
- Practical test automation experience, ideally with ServiceNow ATF, and enough JavaScript to read and write server-side scripts and GlideRecord queries. 
- Strong data validation skills: comfortable reconciling numbers across tables, reports and spreadsheets, and explaining where a figure comes from. 
- Experience writing structured test cases and sign-off reports, and using Jira and a test management tool such as Zephyr. 
- Clear written and spoken English, with the confidence to walk stakeholders through test results and to discuss your own past work in depth. 
Preferred qualifications 
- ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA); a Certified Implementation Specialist in Software Asset Management (CIS-SAM) is a strong plus. 
- Exposure to software licensing models for SaaS and enterprise publishers (named user, subscription, resource or consumption based). 
- Experience testing REST API integrations and vendor usage exports. 
- Familiarity with Agile delivery and ALM tools such as Jira.

title: Senior QA Automation Engineer, Data Visualization and Platform
location: Mexico, Brazil, India, Costa Rica, Honduras, Peru (remote)
description:
ABOUT SIFT

Sift is the data infrastructure platform for hardware engineering teams. Sift turns high-frequency telemetry into engineering insights for mission-critical systems. Teams use Sift to build and operate rockets, satellites, autonomous vehicles, energy systems, defense platforms, and more.

Founded by former SpaceX engineers who built the tools behind Dragon and Starlink, Sift is building the data infrastructure to herald the AI era for physical systems.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Engineers use our data exploration product to plot and investigate live and historical telemetry at high channel counts.

You will own test automation for that product and our GPU-accelerated charting engine, including the move from legacy charts to the new engine. Your job is to catch functional, performance and cross-browser regressions before customers do, and to turn today's partly manual performance testing into repeatable checks in CI. Later, you will also cover our core application layer: access control, navigation, search and the design system. You will report to the Head of Quality Engineering and work embedded with the data visualization team.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU'LL:

 - Own the end-to-end suite. Extend and maintain our Playwright tests for panels, annotations, data sources, sharing and plotting. Keep them fast, stable and trusted.

 - Make E2E a merge gate. Get smoke and critical-path tests running on every pull request, cut flakiness and define what blocks a release.

 - Expand browser coverage. Add Microsoft Edge and Firefox alongside Chrome, with a focus on Windows, where many of our customers work.

 - Automate performance testing. Turn our browser and hardware performance study into repeatable tests with frame-time and lag thresholds, driven by our telemetry simulator at realistic channel counts and data rates.

 - Introduce visual regression checks for charts and panels where they add signal without flakiness.

 - Prove the chart migrations. Build a parity suite that compares each legacy chart view with its new-engine version, across time-series, scatter, histogram, FFT and 3D charts.

 - Cover the core application layer. Map coverage gaps and build regression tests for access control (RBAC and ABAC), service accounts, folders, navigation, the home page, search and the design system.

 - Train and guide a QE in another time zone. Onboard a QE who runs regression overnight, and review their results.

 - Shape quality before code merges. Review test plans with engineers, push for unit test coverage in the web app, and test features before release.

 - Report on quality. Track pass rates, flaky tests and performance trends, and surface regressions quickly to the team.
   


REQUIRED SKILLS:

 - 5+ years in QA automation or SDET roles, with at least 2 years building UI test suites for complex web applications.

 - Strong Playwright and TypeScript skills. You have designed suites, not only written tests: fixtures, test data setup, tagging, parallelization and flake control.

 - Experience running E2E tests in CI, ideally GitHub Actions, as a blocking gate on pull requests.

 - Cross-browser testing experience across Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Firefox on Windows and macOS.

 - Hands-on frontend performance testing: browser DevTools, performance traces, frame rate and rendering analysis.

 - Comfort reading React code and writing unit tests with Vitest or Jest.

 - Experience testing authorization (RBAC and ABAC) and backend APIs, ideally Go services over gRPC.

 - Professional working proficiency in written and spoken English (CEFR B2 or above), used daily for design reviews, test plans, risk reports, working with and training teammates.

 - At least 4 hours a day of overlap with US Pacific time.
   


BONUS POINTS:

 - Testing data visualization, charting or WebGL and canvas-heavy applications.

 - Experience with real-time or streaming data products.

 - Visual regression testing with Playwright screenshots or a similar tool.

 - Python scripting for test data and load generation.

 - Familiarity with telemetry, time-series data or hardware test workflows.

 - Using AI agents to write and maintain tests.

 - Testing software that customers run in their own cloud or on-prem.
   


ENGINEERING AT SIFT:

 - E2E and browser: Playwright, TypeScript

 - Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vitest, Testing Library

 - Backend and API: Go, gRPC, PostgreSQL

 - Integrations and edge: Rust, Python, Protobuf

 - Test data and scripting: Python

 - Streaming: Kafka-compatible event streaming

 - CI: GitHub Actions
   


LOCATION:

This is a remote, full-time-equivalent independent contractor engagement for candidates based in Latin America or the Caribbean. You will work at least 4 hours a day overlapping with US Pacific time and collaborate closely with engineering teams in California.

Compensation range: $4,000 - $4,500 USD per month (Latin America and the Caribbean)

Candidates who advance will complete a standardized English assessment administered by a third-party provider. We will share how your results are used and stored, and request your consent, before the assessment.

description:
**QA Automation Engineer (AI-native)**

Join the Happilee QA team and own one question for every release: is it ready for a real customer, and what is the evidence? You will build the tests, pipelines and checks that answer it, with AI coding agents as everyday tools.

**About the role**

NeoITO (est. 2014) builds AI and commerce systems for enterprises and startups. Happilee is our own product: a no-code WhatsApp Business API platform for marketing, sales and support, built as an official Meta Business Partner. Happilee for Instagram, its newest part, automates comment-to-DM and DM conversations.

Businesses run broadcasts, chatbots, a shared team inbox and subscriptions on Happilee, under our brand and under partners' brands.

The job is deciding what to test, building the automation that tests it, and wiring it into the pipeline so it runs on every change. It also means using the product as a customer does, noticing what works but still feels wrong, and watching production after each release. This is not a role for running someone else's test cases.

Our developers build with AI coding agents every day, so code arrives faster than ever. You will make sure the checks keep up, and you will use the same agents to build them.

**What you will do**

* Turn requirements into test plans before development ends. Read the requirements doc, ask what it leaves out, and cover the combinations that matter: brand, plan, role, feature flag and channel.
* Review every feature as a customer would before it ships: the flow, the wording, loading, empty and error states, small screens, slow networks, and how closely it matches the design.
* Build and own automated suites for UI, API and end-to-end flows, with the test data and fixtures that make them repeatable.
* Build the pipelines that run those suites on each pull request and deploy, so a failing test blocks the merge.
* Run release gates: verify each feature on staging, give a written go/no-go, and smoketest production within minutes of a release.
* Test against real WhatsApp and Instagram accounts, not only mocks.
* Load-test and soak-test the paths that take traffic spikes, such as broadcasts, webhooks and logins, and track memory and errors over long runs.
* Check security basics on each release: authentication on every endpoint, role permissions, keeping each customer's data separate, and input validation.
* Keep a browser and device matrix that matches what customers actually use, including old browsers and slow networks.
* Use AI coding agents to write, refactor and debug test code, and review every line they produce.
* Turn every bug that reaches a customer into a regression test, and write the short note that stops it happening again.

**Must have: testing fundamentals**

* Test design: boundary values, equivalence classes, decision tables, state transitions and pairwise combinations, chosen by risk.
* The test pyramid in practice: what belongs in unit, integration, API and end-to-end tests, and what each costs to run and maintain.
* Exploratory testing with a charter, and bug reports a developer can act on: steps, expected and actual result, evidence, severity and priority.
* Test data and environments: seeding, isolation and cleanup, so no test depends on another test or on shared state.
* Flaky tests: you can find why a test is flaky (timing, ordering, shared data, network) and fix the cause instead of adding retries.
* Code: TypeScript or JavaScript preferred (Java or Python is fine to start), Git and pull requests, and enough SQL to check what the app actually wrote.
* One automation framework in depth. Playwright is preferred; Selenium, Cypress or WebdriverIO count.

**Must have: product and UX sense**

* You follow the whole journey and notice what a customer would trip over: a confusing step, a vague error, a missing loading or empty state, wording only a developer would understand.
* You know common usability heuristics (Nielsen's ten, for example) and accessibility basics (WCAG, keyboard use, contrast), and use them to explain why something is wrong.
* What was built gets checked against the design and the design system: spacing, type, states and behaviour.
* You separate a UX defect from a preference. A defect breaks the design, a heuristic or the user's goal, and comes with evidence; a preference goes to the designer as a suggestion.

**Must have: AI-assisted engineering**

* You use AI coding agents regularly, at work or on your own projects (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot or similar), and can show us something you built with one.
* Prompt engineering: a clear task, constraints, examples and the output you expect, with a plan asked for before any code.
* Context engineering: the agent gets the spec, the right files, the API schema and the project's conventions, and nothing it doesn't need.
* You know when to split a task or start a fresh session. Agent output is a draft. A test is done only when you have watched it fail against broken code and pass against working code.
* Tests are checked against the requirement, not only the code. An agent that writes both the code and its tests can make them agree while both are wrong.

**Strong plus**

Nobody has all of this. Bring some of it, and the appetite to learn the rest.

* Highly preferred: a test pipeline you built end to end, from test design to suites, test data, a CI run and a readable report, at work or on your own.
* API testing: Postman or Bruno, Playwright's request API or supertest; contract and schema tests from OpenAPI; webhook signatures, retries and idempotency.
* Load and performance: k6, JMeter, Gatling, Artillery or Locust; a realistic load model; p95 and p99 latency, error rates and memory over a long soak.
* Security testing: OWASP Top 10 and API Top 10, Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP, accesscontrol checks, keeping customers' data apart.
* CI/CD and environments: GitHub Actions or similar, Docker and Docker Compose for test environments, basic Linux, reading cloud logs.
* Development: code you have shipped (a feature, a fix, a side project), a stack trace followed to the line, a fix proposed along with the bug. Node.js and React help.
* How agents work underneath: tools, MCP servers (for example Playwright MCP), subagents, hallucination and token cost.
* Design and UX depth: Figma, visual regression against design baselines, automated accessibility checks (axe), screen-reader testing, usability sessions with real users, and multi-language UI, including right-to-left.
* Also welcome: Sentry, Grafana and synthetic monitoring; the WhatsApp Business and Instagram Messaging APIs and Meta webhooks; payment gateways in test mode; evaluating LLM output with golden sets and rubrics.

description:
#### **Overview**

Founded in 1988, Trimont (www.trimont.com) is a specialized global commercial real estate loan services provider and partner for lenders and investors seeking the infrastructure and capabilities needed to help them scale their business and make informed, effective decisions related to the deployment, management and administration of commercial real estate secured credit. As the largest master servicer of commercial real estate loans in the United States, Trimont manages securitizations with meticulous oversight and coordination—protecting cash flows, mitigating risk, and ensuring portfolio performance.

TriVinna, a Trimont company, is rebuilding commercial real estate lending software from the ground up. For decades, CRE lenders have run trillion-dollar portfolios on fragmented legacy systems, disconnected spreadsheets, and manual re-keying of borrower financials, rent rolls, and loan events. Leveraging Trimont’s access to approximately 11% of all U.S. commercial real estate lending data and nearly four decades of servicing expertise, we are building an AI-native platform that captures loan data at the source, unifies it across the full loan lifecycle, and turns it into decisions lenders can act on.

TriVinna is an innovative firm where visionary professionals come to learn, grow, and thrive with colleagues driven by curiosity and collaboration.

* **Learn:** We believe ongoing learning is critical and are focused on providing a work environment where all team members can take ownership of their careers.
* **Grow:** We work alongside the largest institutional lenders in the world, overseeing the most significant projects in the industry. This unique opportunity allows us to broaden our skillset and develop our abilities by tackling some of the industry’s most challenging and exciting endeavors.
* **Thrive:** Our firm is a place where ethics and excellence meet to create an experience that matches our capabilities. There are no limits to what we as team members and as an organization, can achieve together.

*Where people, purpose, and progress come together every day.*

#### **Job Summary**

TriVinna is seeking a Senior QA Engineer to own the depth and quality of testing for the products that are replacing the legacy tools CRE lenders have relied on for decades. Our multi-service .NET platform handles loan review and servicing for institutional lenders, and when a lender imports a rent roll or approves a loan action, the result has to be right.

You will design each product’s tests, build them with a coding agent, and keep them valid as the products change. You will report to the QA Lead, who sets how testing works across the platform, and you will make it work for your products. Your job is to pair close knowledge of those products with sharp judgment about what the agent wrote, so that a passing test means the product works.

#### **Key Responsibilities**

**What you’ll work on**

* **Browser tests:** Playwright and TypeScript journeys through each product’s React screens.
* **Workflow and API tests:** flows that cross services, such as a rent roll import through review and approval.
* **Access tests:** which roles can reach which endpoints and data, across organizations and sub-organizations.
* **Test data:** the files and seeded records each feature’s tests need, with the values a correct result produces.
* **Tests in the pipeline:** your tests run in CI against a fresh environment for each feature, not only on a laptop.
* **Failed runs:** telling a product fault from a faulty test, and keeping the tests reliable.

**Examples of work you’d own end to end**

* Review a new feature’s requirements, list what can’t be tested as written, and plan its tests before work starts.
* Write the browser journey for a document upload: import a rent roll, check the values it produced against the expected ones, and take it through approval.
* Build access tests for a service: every role against every endpoint, allowed or refused.
* Investigate a failed overnight run, decide whether the product or the test is at fault, then file the bug or fix the test.
* Get a new test running at the right stage of the pipeline, and debug it when it fails only in CI.
* Fix the tests after an intended UI change, as a pull request.
* Add a test for a bug that reached users, and show that it fails without the fix.

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 5-12 years testing software products, including test automation with Playwright and TypeScript.
* Experience owning a product’s tests end to end, from a feature’s requirements to its test design, the tests themselves, their data, and the failures they raise.
* Real experience with coding agents in testing: you can describe a test an agent wrote that passed for the wrong reason, and how you caught it.

**Expert (you could teach it)**

* Test design: turning requirements into cases that cover the behavior, its boundaries, and its failure paths, and knowing which are worth automating.
* Playwright and TypeScript: browser journeys, fixtures, locators that survive UI changes, tracing, and debugging a flaky test.
* Reading a failure: telling a product fault from a faulty test, and a test that proves behavior from one that only passes.

**Strong (you do it independently)**

* API testing: HTTP, authentication, tokens and roles, and request and response contracts.
* Test data design: seeded organizations, users, and roles, and input files with known expected results.
* Tests in CI: GitHub Actions, tests selected by tag, reading a failed run, and telling an environment problem from a test problem.
* Bug reports a developer can act on: steps, evidence, expected, and actual.

**Working knowledge (you deliver, with some lookup)**

* C# and .NET, enough to follow an endpoint to its permission check.
* SQL, enough to check what a workflow wrote.
* Accessibility checks and screenshot comparisons.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in commercial real estate lending or servicing.
* Experience testing spreadsheet and document imports.
* Contract testing and exploratory testing.

#### **How We Work**

**With agents**

* You use a coding agent to write most of the test code, and you treat the output as a draft.
* You check every generated assertion against the requirement. A test has to fail when the behavior is wrong.
* You give the agent the right context: the requirement, the screen or endpoint, the test data, and how the existing tests are written.
* You never paste secrets or customer data into a tool, and test data never comes from production.

**With the team**

* You review requirements before work starts, and ask questions until a feature is testable.
* Collaborate with data engineers to curate accurate data schemas and manage data quality in the test environment.
* You send each failure to whoever can fix it, with what they need to reproduce it.
* You work to the standards the QA Lead sets, and tell the lead where they don’t fit your products.
* Developers write unit tests and the tests for their own code; you own the tests of the running product.
* You raise a blocker the day you see it, in writing, with what’s blocked, what you tried, and what you need.
* You say up front when a feature’s testing won’t fit its schedule.

#### **Why This Role**

Commercial real estate lending is one of the largest asset classes in the world, and it still runs on software built for a different era. The software that replaces it has to be trusted with every number. This is a rare chance to be the person who makes sure it is, backed by the data, client relationships, and operational expertise of the largest master servicer in the United States.

* **Own real quality.** Be the reason lenders can trust what TriVinna’s products produce.
* **Work at the frontier.** Test in one of the most advanced AI-assisted engineering practices in financial services.
* **Learn the domain.** Build deep knowledge of CRE lending through the workflows you test.
* **Work with the industry’s leaders.** Your work will support some of the largest institutional lenders and investors in commercial real estate.

Trimont and TriVinna are equal opportunity employers, and we’re proud to support and celebrate diversity in the workplace. If you have a disability and need an accommodation or assistance with the application process and/or using our website, please contact us. We are proud to maintain a drug-free policy, ensuring that our community is a secure and productive space for all our team members.
